components.html:

components.css: .ds-ticket { display: block; background: oklch(0.16 0.010 330); border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklch, var(--mode) 30%, oklch(0.28 0.014 330)); border-radius: 10px; padding: 18px 20px; text-decoration: none; position: relative; transition: border-color .15s cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1), transform .15s cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1), background .15s cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-ticket:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); background: oklch(0.21 0.012 330); } .ds-ticket:active { transform: translateY(-2px) scale(0.99); transition-duration: .1s; } .ds-ticket-head { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; margin-bottom: 14px; } .ds-ticket-mode { font-family: 'Manrope', sans-serif; font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 1.3px; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--mode); display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; } .ds-live-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--mode); } .ds-ticket-state { font-family: 'Manrope', sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; padding: 2px 9px; border-radius: 3px; text-transform: uppercase; background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--mode) 14%, transparent); color: var(--mode); border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklch, var(--mode) 32%, transparent); } .ds-ticket-body { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-weight: 700; font-size: 20px; color: oklch(0.95 0.006 330); text-align: center; padding: 8px 0; }

narrative.overview:
CoC Analytics reads as a thermal-scope readout, not a SaaS dashboard: a near-black gunmetal surface that everything else sits on top of, with color reserved for signal, not decoration. Two hues carry the identify-friend-or-foe logic that the whole page runs on — Threat Magenta flags urgency and primary interaction, IFF Green flags a positive or friendly result — and a small family of category hues (War Amber, Raid Red, CWL Violet, Recon Blue) let a clan leader tell which mode a card belongs to at a glance, without reading the label first. This is a product surface (PRODUCT.md), not a brand page: the system exists to serve fast, trustworthy verdicts for two audiences at once — the leader making a bench call and the member checking their own week — never to perform for its own sake.

What this system explicitly rejects, per PRODUCT.md's anti-references: the flattened, generic bordered-stat-tile SaaS-dashboard cliché, and anything that reads as a cold, soulless spreadsheet. Precision is the personality here, not sterility — the page should invite clicking around, not feel like a data dump.
keyCharacteristics: Committed color strategy on identity-driven surfaces: Threat Magenta carries real visual weight, not a 10%-of-screen accent dab.
Flat by default — depth comes from tonal layering (bg → surface → raised surface), not drop shadows.
One shared easing curve and a complete hover → focus → active state chain on every interactive card; quiet at rest, decisive on interaction.

A strict two-tier information hierarchy wherever a section would otherwise become a flat repeated grid: a small set of featured, live-aware cards, plus a visually quieter compact-row tier for everything secondary.

rules.name: The One Hue, One Job Rule
rules.body: Threat Magenta means "interactive or primary," never "this belongs to War." War, Raid, CWL, and Ranked each carry their own dedicated hue so a color never has to answer two different questions at once.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth is bg → surface → raised-surface, not shadow. If an element needs to read as "above" its neighbor, step it one tonal level up; reach for box-shadow only on floating overlay chrome that genuinely leaves the document flow.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Any value a user reads as data — a score, a count, a stat — renders in JetBrains Mono, full stop. Manrope carries everything else.

rules.name: The Flat Deck Rule
rules.body: Cards never cast a shadow to prove they're clickable. A card's clickability is carried by its border, its hover tonal-shift, and its cursor — not by pretending it's floating above the surface it's actually flush with.

dos: Do use OKLCH for every color token — no hex, no HSL.
Do give every game mode its own dedicated hue, distinct from Threat Magenta.
Do carry a verdict, not just a number, wherever the underlying logic supports one.
Do give every interactive card the full state chain: resting, hover, focus-visible, active/press.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion for every transform-based hover/press effect and the live-dot pulse.
Do reuse the Compact Row component wherever a section needs a quiet secondary tier.
donts: Don't use a border-left/border-right stripe greater than 1px as a colored accent on any card, list item, or nav-active state.
Don't use background-clip: text gradient text for any heading.
Don't reach for a drop shadow to make a card read as elevated or clickable.
Don't build a flat grid of 6+ identically-shaped icon+heading+text cards.
Don't let raw text emoji stand in for an icon anywhere.
Don't let Threat Magenta answer more than one question on a single screen.
Don't ship a hover-only interaction with no keyboard equivalent.
